# Ichkerian war crimes

}}During the existence of the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria, Chechen rebels committed war crimes against the Russian civilians and Russians POWs.
Background
After the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria declared its independence from the Russian Federation, reports were made by the Russian civilians living in Chechnya that Chechen Forces were killing the civilians, and looting homes from the non-Chechen population.
Following the election of Dzhokhar Dudayev in 1991, the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria was an autocratic state with chaos and abuse against non-Chechens, particularly Russians. Russian civilians were beaten, humiliated, kidnapped, robbed and even killed, which resulted in 20,000 Russians fleeing the country.
During the 1990s, various Russian civilians also claimed to have gotten threatening letters telling them to leave the country.
Russian women and men began disappearing during 1991 and 1992, which resulted in the Russians writing letters to Boris Yeltsin urging him to help them. The letters talked about how Russian families were found killed, and houses being taken away from them by Chechen Forces.
More than 21,000 Russians were killed by Chechen Forces and 46,000 were enslaved and killed later, with 90,000 being expelled from Chechnya.
Chechen Wars 1994-2000
In 1994, Russia invaded the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria, killing civilians on purpose to scare the Chechens, and didn't hold back. This sparked a hatred and vengeance among the rebel forces.
During the war, Chechen soldiers used guerilla tactics and exploited the Russian Army's weaknesses and outsmarted them by surrounding the soldiers.
Chechen soldiers executed many POWs by beheadings, most notably Yevgeny Rodionov, and also targeted Russian civilians during the war. There was also the Tukhchar massacre, which took place in the Dagestan village of Tukhchar, where Chechen rebels executed five soldiers and one officer.
Chechen soldiers also targeted Russian civilians during the First Chechen War, which resulted in the death of 35,000 Russian civilians whereas 24,000 to 25,500 Russian civilians were killed by the Russians.
Death toll
An estimated 21,000 Russian civilians including 46,000 slaves were killed before and after the wars while 35,000 were killed during the First Chechen War.
